title: Tenant-graded fuse + safe reroute orchestration for model/dependency failures
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-scoped, graded "fuse" (circuit) system that trips progressively based on dependency/model/region health and SLO burn, enabling safe automated reroutes and prioritized load-shedding without causing cascades.

Background: Current coarse-grained breakers are reactive and blunt: they trip whole model endpoints, causing large customer impact and expensive failovers. We need a finer control plane that can: (1) reason per-tenant and per-model, (2) use SLO-aware thresholds (burn-rate + latency tail), and (3) apply staged fallbacks that preserve privacy and correctness where required.

Proposed design (high level):
- Metrics & signals: maintain per-tenant/per-model sliding-window error rate, 95/99 latency EWMA, and SLO burn-rate over multiple windows (1m/5m/1h). Also track region-level capacity and dependency error profiles (KV store, auth, infra deps).
- Graded trips: three levels: "soft-tripped" (start shedding low-priority traffic and route to cheaper variants), "probation" (partial traffic diversion + accelerated monitoring), "hard-tripped" (block or reroute all non-critical requests). Use hysteresis windows and minimum hold times to avoid flapping.
- Dynamic thresholds: base thresholds come from SLOs (e.g., error budget burn-rate > 4x triggers soft trip). Thresholds scale by tenant priority weight and model criticality. Low-priority tenants get earlier soft-trips.
- Fallback hierarchy (safe-by-default): 1) cached valid response (TTL + cache-qualification checks), 2) quantized/local proxy variant (lower-cost model with preserved lineage/labels), 3) verified fallback open model with output filters, 4) feature-degraded response (strip optional fields), 5) hard reject with structured error and user-facing guidance. For private/VPC tenants we block any fallback that leaks data outside tenant boundary — fallback will be limited to on-prem or same-VPC variants.
- Multi-region failover: region health aggregator computes region safety score. On regional degradation, orchestrator probabilistically shifts traffic to warm regions with capacity-aware caps. Cross-region reroutes respect data locality flags; if data locality forbids, escalate to manual runbook.
- Load-shedding policy: global prioritized shedding buckets: realtime low-latency paths (highest), background batch/async (lowest). Shedding uses token-bucket allowance combined with tenant weight to proportionally throttle.
- Safety & observability: all fallback decisions emit a single canonical event (trace id, reason, defender rule id) to tracing and a dedicated "fuse.events" metric stream. Dashboards to show per-tenant trip state, SLO burn, fallback counts, cost delta, and rollback controls in Console.

Implementation notes:
- Fuse evaluator implemented as stateless actor with consistent hashing to owner node; state persisted in a small bounded store (Redis) with versioned keys to allow feature flags.
- Use EWMA + windowed counters for smooth signals; use reservoir sampling for 99th latency.
- Provide admission hooks in the runtime router that check the fuse state before scheduling on GPU; implement fast-path for cached responses.
- Feature-flag the new evaluator behind runtime feature "tenant_fuse_v2" and a Console toggle per-customer.

Testing & rollout plan:
1) Unit tests for threshold math and hysteresis. 2) Integration tests using local runtime and injected dependency faults (auth error spikes, KV latency). 3) Chaos runbook: simulate region network partition and verify probabilistic reroute, then measure SLO compliance. 4) Canary rollout: internal tenants -> 5 low-risk customers (10%) -> 50% -> all, with ability to rollback instantly.

Acceptance criteria:
- No customer sees >5% additional 5xx error rate attributable to new logic during canary.
- Soft-trips show expected gradient by tenant weight in staged experiments.
- Dashboard surfaces trip reason and affected requests within 30s.
- Runbook validated: on region hard-trip we can re-route 95% of eligible traffic to warm regions without violating data locality flags.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-redwood/design/tenant-graded-fuse
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7123
- Observability dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood/company/d/qwerty/fuse-overview

Risks and mitigations:
- Cache staleness: ensure cache qualification step and TTL policy; add cache-bypass header for sensitive reads.
- Cost spike from reroutes to larger models: put cost-budget caps and auto-escalation to manual approval for unbounded cost.
- Privacy leakage: default to blocking cross-boundary fallbacks for private tenants; include gating tests.

Next steps: finish prototype PR reviews, add QA scenarios for private deployments, extend Console UI to show per-tenant trip thresholds and manual override controls.
comments: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on graded trip levels and SLO-driven thresholds. Action: Miguel to prototype EWMA-based latency tracking; Priya to own UX for Console overrides.

2026-02-22: Prototype complete. Initial results: soft-trip stopped 28% of low-priority requests under simulated model instability with negligible impact on P95 for high-priority tenants. Uploaded microbench results to the design doc.
2026-02-28: Design review feedback from Priya Raman — request to expose tenant weight in Console and to add a 'simulate trip' button for support. Added to scope.
2026-03-04: Security review asked for explicit rule: no cross-tenant/data-plane fallbacks for private/VPC deployments. Confirmed; added gating logic and tests.

2026-03-08: Miguel opened prototype PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7123. QA flagged cache qualification bug (cache returned stale timestamp for zero-ttl). Miguel fixed in PR branch.
2026-03-10: Load test results: multi-region reroute increased cross-region egress cost by 4% but kept tenant SLOs within target. Decision: add cost caps per-tenant before broad rollout.
2026-03-12: Code review done; merging to staging. Next: schedule chaos test and canary with internal tenants next week.
